text: Events + covered length per node.

The sweep line (扫描线) turns a 2D problem into many 1D ones. For the area of a union of rectangles, sweep a vertical line from left to right. Each rectangle becomes two events: at x1 add +1 on its y-interval, at x2 add −1. Between two consecutive events the covered length on the line stays constant, so area += covered length × Δx (P5490).

A segment tree over the (discretised) y-coordinates stores, per node, cnt = how many whole rectangles cover the node's interval, and len = covered length inside it. No lazy push is needed: if cnt > 0 the whole interval is covered, else len = sum of the children. Every +1 has a matching −1, which is why this works.

Leaf i of the tree stands for the y-interval [ys[i], ys[i+1]], so a rectangle [y1, y2] updates leaves a … b − 1. The answer is checked against a Python grid count over the compressed coordinates. The same sweep counts points in rectangles (offline with a Fenwick tree) and computes union perimeters.
Best line at the midpoint; loser goes one way.

A Li Chao tree (李超线段树) stores lines y = kx + b and answers "the maximum (or minimum) value at x" in O(log C). Each node keeps the line that is best at its midpoint. When a new line arrives, compare at the midpoint and swap so the better one stays; the loser can only win on one side, so push it into that child only.

That "one side only" fact makes insertion O(log C) instead of touching both halves. It is the general replacement for the convex hull trick (进阶篇第18章): lines may arrive in any order and queries can be anywhere. Segments (P4097) are inserted into O(log C) nodes first.

Answers checked against a Python maximum over all lines. Nodes are created on demand, so the x-range can be wide without a big array.
mid must round consistently for negative ranges: l + (r − l) / 2 does. For minimum queries flip every comparison.
Dynamic value trees merged up the tree.

Segment tree merging (线段树合并): give every tree node its own dynamic value segment tree (created on demand). To combine children into a parent, merge their trees: walk both at once; where only one has a node, take it as it is; where both have a node, merge their children recursively and pull up.

Each merge step destroys one node, so all merges together cost the total number of nodes created: O(n log V). It answers "for every subtree" questions about value distributions (most frequent value, k-th smallest), and with tree differences, path updates (雨天的尾巴 P4556).
For each node: the most frequent value in its subtree (smallest on ties). Checked against a Python count of every subtree.
ans[u] must be read right after u's merges: later, u's tree is reused inside its parent's tree and changes. If answers are needed later, store them immediately (as here) or copy nodes when merging.
Heap by value, BST by index, stack build.

A Cartesian tree (笛卡尔树) of an array: the root is the position of the minimum; the left subtree is built from the part to its left, the right from the part to its right. It is a heap by value and a BST by index. Build it in O(n) with a stack holding the rightmost chain.

Range minimum of [l, r] = the LCA of l and r in this tree. "For each element, the maximal range where it is the minimum" is exactly its subtree, which is the same information a monotonic stack gives (largest rectangle in a histogram, counting subarrays by their minimum).
